name: delta-fee-rate-change
pattern: delta would <merchant> pay if the relative fee
operation: fees under a rule with its rate replaced, minus fees under the rule as is
invariant: delta is linear in (new − old) rate; an unchanged rate gives 0

guidelines.guideline: Answer must be just a number rounded to 14 decimals. If a question does not have a relevant or applicable answer for the task, please respond with 'Not Applicable'

canonical_method.helper: fee_total_for_rule(rule, transactions, account_type, mcc, capture_delay, monthly_fraud_level, monthly_volume, rate=<override>)
steps: rule = next(f for f in fees if f['ID']==id)

for each month touching the period: stats = monthly_merchant_stats(...); current = fee_total_for_rule(rule, stats['transactions'], ..., ); new = fee_total_for_rule(rule, stats['transactions'], ..., rate=new_rate)
delta = sum(new - current) across months, rounded to 14 decimals

pitfalls: Check whether the rule's current rate already equals the proposed new rate first (task 2484) — delta is legitimately 0.0 in that case, don't treat it as an error
Must iterate per month like F01/F03 since the rule's monthly_fraud_level match (and hence whether it applies at all) can differ month to month within a year period

few_shot.question: In the year 2023 what delta would Crossfit_Hanna pay if the relative fee of the fee with ID=792 changed to 1?
few_shot.code: helper.fee_total_for_rule(rule_792, matching_txns, rate=1) - helper.fee_total_for_rule(rule_792, matching_txns, rate=83)

prompt_rule: if the question asks the fee delta from changing a named rule's rate → fee_total_for_rule with and without rate= override, iterate months if the period spans more than one, sum the deltas; format: number rounded to 14 decimals.
note: Dev anchor 1871 already validates this family end-to-end; keep it in the McNemar gate set as regression insurance.
